LHX.sentence: L3Harris has drifted down to about 27% below its high, which is unusually deep for a steady defense contractor, but nothing has really changed — military spending is still a reliable tailwind.

ASML.sentence: ASML keeps climbing and sits near the top of its range, which makes sense for the only company in the world that makes a certain kind of chipmaking machine.

LIN.sentence: Linde is quiet this week — industrial gas demand is steady and they nudge prices up a little each quarter, which is pretty much the whole story with this one.

MSFT.sentence: Microsoft slipped a touch, but it's actually been leading the big tech names lately as its cloud and AI business keeps grinding along without drama.

TMO.sentence: Thermo Fisher is steady — demand from labs and biotech slowed to a crawl but looks to be bottoming out and picking back up, which is the part that matters for them.

CVX.sentence: Chevron is steady, but remember its profits are puffed up right now because Middle East tensions have pushed oil far above normal — that's the oil price doing the work, not the company itself, so don't read today's fat profits as the business getting better.

NOW.sentence: ServiceNow jumped a bit but is still way off its high, even as big companies and government agencies keep signing up for its software that automates office busywork with AI assistants.

GLNCY.sentence: Glencore eased off a little, with copper prices running slightly ahead of the stock — this is a company that both mines metals and runs the world's biggest commodity trading desk.

MLM.sentence: Martin Marietta eased back slightly, but the price it gets per ton of crushed stone is still creeping up — a reported price dip was just a mix of what sold, not the business weakening.

KOF.sentence: This Latin American Coca-Cola bottler is basically flat, though a weaker Mexican peso quietly eats into earnings since most of its money is earned in pesos but reported in dollars.

UBER.sentence: Uber ticked up, and people keep booking more and more rides and food orders through the app — the big open question is just how the self-driving car companies will play out down the road.

AMKBY.sentence: Maersk, the Danish container-shipping giant, fell a bit but is trading below what its fleet of ships would cost to replace — an unusually cheap level that tends to put a floor under the stock.

MA.sentence: Mastercard was flat — people keep tapping their cards more than ever, and there's no real crack in the business, just the usual long-term worry about new payment technology someday cutting out the card networks.

ISRG.sentence: The surgical robot maker slipped slightly and is now meaningfully cheaper than its own recent norm, even as hospitals keep doing more operations with its machines and buying the supplies each one uses.

NVDA.sentence: Nvidia bounced back up, but the real question now is whether its handful of giant customers — Google and Amazon among them — can keep paying for all the computing gear they buy, since two of them are now spending more than they earn and borrowing the rest.
